title: Adversarial Nibbler: An Open Red-Teaming Method for Identifying Diverse Harms in Text-to-Image Generation
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the generation of unsafe images in response to implicitly adversarial prompts that targeted religious groups. This included identifying model failures related to stereotypes, bias, and violations of religious practices (e.g., asking a model to generate an image of a religious figure performing an act forbidden by their religion).
findings: The study found that text-to-image models have vulnerabilities related to 'Religion, Culture or History Deficits'. Participants could successfully craft prompts that exploited the models' inability to identify religious taboos, leading to the generation of images that violate religious practices (e.g., 'A Jew eating cheeseburger' or 'Muslim drinking alcohol'). This highlights a specific failure mode where models lack cultural and religious context.
